title: Exact smooth pullback of quasi-coherent modules on algebraic stacks
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$ be a smooth morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], where smoothness is tested on smooth scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Give their quasi-coherent module categories the big-fppf conventions of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and their abelian structures [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-abelian]. Then tensor pullback $f^*:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$ is an exact functor: it carries each short exact sequence in the source abelian category to a short exact sequence in the target abelian category. If $\mathcal Z=T$ is a scheme, the functor $F\mapsto F_f$ to quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-modules from [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] is exact, including preservation of kernels, cokernels and monomorphisms in these categories. No quasi-compactness, finite-generation, representability or Noetherian assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 076X (lemma-flat-pullback-quasi-coherent), smooth specialization by chartwise smooth-flatness; Tag 0GQF (lemma-quasi-coherent-check-exact), proof, faithful exact scheme-chart restrictions; stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 075U (definition-smooth).

proof.text: First fix any smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:U\to\mathcal Y$ of an algebraic stack. On etale scheme charts it is flat and locally of finite presentation by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion]. By [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations](2), $R=U\times_{\mathcal Y}U$ is its flat groupoid relation and $[U/R]\to\mathcal Y$ is an equivalence commuting with $a$; precomposition with it and with a quasi-inverse is tensor pullback by [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], so it identifies the quasi-coherent categories, compatibly with restriction to $U$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-groupoid-module-descent] and then [lem-sfb-flat-space-groupoid-kernels-cokernels]: $\Phi:F\mapsto x^*F|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}$, for the canonical $x:U\to[U/R]$ identified with $a$, is additive and faithful and carries kernels and cokernels to the small-etale module kernels and cokernels. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], $\Phi(F)$ is $u\mapsto\Gamma(U',u^*F_a)$ on etale $u:U'\to U$, naturally in $F$, i.e. $\Phi=A_U\circ\Psi$ for $\Psi:F\mapsto F_a$ and the associated-sheaf functor $A_U$ of [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. $A_U$ is exact into all etale module sheaves by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison], and its restriction to Zariski opens is the identity, so $A_U$ reflects isomorphisms. Hence $\Psi$ is faithful, and for $h$ in $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Y)$ the comparison maps from $\Psi(\ker h)$ to the Zariski kernel of $\Psi(h)$, and from the Zariski cokernel of $\Psi(h)$ to $\Psi(\operatorname{coker}h)$, become isomorphisms after $A_U$, so are isomorphisms. Thus $F\mapsto F_a$ computes kernels and cokernels and is faithful and exact. The abelian structure here is that of [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-abelian], since kernels and cokernels are determined by their universal properties, which equivalences preserve.

source.place: 076X (lemma-flat-pullback-quasi-coherent), faithful exact vertical functors; 06WV and 06VZ expanded

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $b:V\to\mathcal X$ using [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. The stack $\mathcal P=\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal X}V$ is algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], so choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $u:U\to\mathcal P$. Base change and composition of representable smooth surjections in [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus] show that $a:U\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth surjective. Write $q:U\to V$. The defining condition (A) of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion], applied to the smooth $f$ and the smooth map $U\to\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal X}V$, shows that $q$ is a smooth scheme morphism. Therefore $q$ is flat by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion]. This construction never assumes that $f$ is representable.

source.place: 076X, construction of the commutative scheme-chart square; 075U and 06FM

proof.text: Let $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ be short exact in $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)$. Step 1 makes its restriction along $b$ short exact in quasi-coherent Zariski modules on $V$. The ordinary module-sheaf kernel and cokernel remain quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. Their universal properties also hold in the full quasi-coherent subcategory, so this is a short exact sequence of ordinary module sheaves. Flat scheme pullback $q^*$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective]. The natural scheme-test comparisons of [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] identify $q^*F_b$ with $(f^*F)_a$, and likewise for $F',F''$ and their arrows: on a test over $U$, precomposition sends it to the same object over $\mathcal X$ by the square's specified two-isomorphism. The cited identity and composition compatibilities identify both arrows of the sequence, not merely its three objects. Consequently the restriction along $a$ of the pulled-back sequence is short exact.

source.place: 076X, exactness of the top scheme pullback and the commuting pullback diagram

proof.text: Restriction along $a$ preserves kernels and cokernels and is faithful by step 1. A faithful additive functor detects zero objects: if it sends $H$ to zero, it sends $1_H$ to zero, hence $1_H=0$. Apply this to the kernel of the first arrow, the cokernel of the last arrow, and the middle homology $\ker(v)/\operatorname{im}(w)$ of the pulled-back sequence. Images are kernels of cokernels, so their formation also commutes with restriction. Step 3 makes these three restricted objects zero; hence they were zero before restriction. This proves short exactness in $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$, and proves exactness of $f^*$. Additivity is also seen on the faithful atlas: its composite is the additive functor $q^*$ after the additive restriction along $b$.

source.place: 076X, final sentence “Thus we win”, with faithful-exact reflection written out

proof.text: When $\mathcal Z=T$ is a scheme, [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence] identifies $\operatorname{QCoh}(T)$ on the big fppf site with quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-modules. Its inverse is restriction to opens. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], composing this inverse with $f^*$ is precisely $F\mapsto F_f$. The equivalence and its inverse carry kernels and cokernels to kernels and cokernels, directly by the Hom universal properties; therefore this composite is exact. To spell out kernel preservation for an exact additive functor $E$, factor any arrow $h$ through its image and apply $E$ to $0\to\ker h\to\operatorname{dom}h\to\operatorname{im}h\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}h\to\operatorname{cod}h\to\operatorname{coker}h\to0$. The second sequence makes $E(\operatorname{im}h)\to E(\operatorname{cod}h)$ monic, and the first identifies its composite's kernel with $E(\ker h)$; dually the cokernel is $E(\operatorname{coker}h)$. A monomorphism has zero kernel, which is preserved, so monomorphisms are preserved as well. All constructions used arbitrary small atlases and arbitrary quasi-coherent modules.
